question: The Ministry of Agriculture and Farmer's Welfare of India has declared a day of every year as 'National Women's Farmer's Day' on:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Tue Oct 15 2024 00:00:00 GMT+0530 (India Standard Time)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• National Women's Farmer's Day, also known as **Rashtriya Mahila Kisan Diwas**, is celebrated in India on **October 15th** every year.
 
• The day aims to **recognize and honor the contribution of women farmers** in the agriculture sector.
 
• Women farmers constitute nearly **33% of the agricultural labor force** and 48% of the self-employed farmers in India.
 
• The Ministry of Agriculture and Farmer's Welfare of India organizes events and programs to **highlight the achievements and challenges of women farmers** on this day.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Importance of Women in Agriculture:**

 
 
• Women play a vital role in various agricultural activities such as sowing, weeding, harvesting, and post-harvest management.
 
• They also contribute significantly to livestock management and dairy production.
 
• Despite their crucial role, women farmers often face challenges such as limited access to resources, land, and credit facilities.
 
 
 
• **Initiatives for Women Farmers:**
 
 
• The Indian government has launched several schemes to support women farmers, including the Mahila Kisan Sashaktikaran Pariyojana (MKSP).
 
• MKSP aims to empower women in agriculture by promoting sustainable agricultural practices and enhancing their participation in decision-making processes.
 
• Other initiatives include training programs, financial support, and the formation of women self-help groups (SHGs).
 
 
 
• **Challenges Faced by Women Farmers:**
 
 
• Limited access to land ownership and inheritance rights.
 
• Inadequate access to credit and financial services.
 
• Limited availability of training and extension services tailored to women’s needs.
 
• Socio-cultural barriers and gender biases in the agricultural sector.
 
 
 
• **Global Perspective:**
 
 
• Globally, women constitute a significant portion of the agricultural workforce, especially in developing countries.
 
• International organizations such as FAO and UN Women advocate for gender equality in agriculture and the empowerment of women farmers.
 
• These organizations emphasize the need for inclusive policies and programs to address the unique challenges faced by women in agriculture.
